key_insight: Replaying real-world events in chronological order creates a grounded simulation that lets agents forecast beyond their knowledge cutoff and be evaluated on how well they adapt as new information arrives.
problem_solved: Current benchmarks lack temporally grounded, realistic scenarios to measure an agent's ability to adapt and forecast under streaming, open-ended real-world information; FutureSim fills this gap.
method: Build a grounded simulator that chronologically replays real-world events (news articles, questions, and event resolutions).
Let agents interact with the replay while forced to forecast outcomes beyond their knowledge cutoff and update decisions as new events arrive.
Measure performance with outcome-based metrics (forecast accuracy, adaptation speed, and robustness to delayed/novel information).
impact: Provides practitioners a realistic evaluation framework to benchmark and improve agents' online adaptation, long-horizon forecasting, and deployment readiness in dynamic real-world settings.
visual_elements: Timeline replay diagram: chronological stream of real news/events feeding into the simulator.
Agent interaction loop: agent makes forecasts, receives updates, and revises actions—shown as a cyclical flowchart.
Forecast vs. outcome chart: accuracy over time and after updates to show adaptation speed.
Evaluation dashboard mockup: metrics (accuracy, adaptation latency, robustness) and leaderboards comparing agents.
paper_title: FutureSim: Replaying World Events to Evaluate Adaptive Agents
paper_authors: Shashwat Goel, Nikhil Chandak, Arvindh Arun, Ameya Prabhu, Steffen Staab
